# Was Rakuten Securities hacked?

**Confirmed.** Yes, by the company's own account: it says a third party gained unauthorized access to its systems and information in a test environment may have leaked on Nov 11. How the attacker got in and who it was are not established.

Incident: Rakuten Securities breach, Nov 2026. Also reported as Rakuten Securities data leak, Rakuten Securities unauthorized access and 楽天証券 情報漏えい. First published Nov 21, 2026; last updated Nov 21, 2026, 2:50 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Rakuten Securities, Rakuten Group, Japan's Financial Services Agency, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 21, 2026, 2:50 PM ET: **The financial services minister says the agency is working with the police and Japan's cybersecurity office, a report says.** Added s014 ITmedia NEWS (Tier 2, Nov 20): it reports the financial services minister said the agency is working closely with the police and Japan's National Cybersecurity Office, and has asked Rakuten Securities to check any reported fraudulent trade at once and report it. Added to c008 (stays Confirmed) and timeline t009. No new company notice or news release since Nov 19, no FSA page, no published cause, attacker, ransom claim, compensation or count change. c007 stays Reported. No leak site, dark-web page or tracker visited. Privacy check done: no names of officials, reporters, experts or lawyers, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. Rakuten Securities says up to about 15.72 million accounts may be affected, about 4.47 million with personal and financial details. Press calls it the largest breach at a Japanese securities firm so far.
- Who is affected: Current and former Rakuten Securities customers. The company says it has identified them and will tell them individually; it urges caution about phishing and suggests setting a passkey.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 15.72M | Accounts, at most | 4.47M with details plus 11.25M with IDs only, per the company and press |
| 4.47M | Accounts with personal/financial data | Per the company, maximum |
| Nov 11 | Date data may have leaked | Per the company |

### Known so far

- Rakuten Securities says a third party gained unauthorized access to some of its systems, detected on Nov 16.
- It says information in its test environment may have leaked on Nov 11.
- It says up to about 4.47 million accounts had personal and financial details exposed, including birth dates, addresses and withdrawal bank accounts.
- It says it has not confirmed any password or PIN leak, or related unauthorized trades.
- The company says it used real customer data, not dummy data, in the test environment, the press reports.
- Japan's Financial Services Agency ordered the company to report on Nov 19.

### Not known yet

- How the attacker got in, and what flaw was used.
- Who did it.
- Whether anyone has claimed a ransom or published the data.
- Whether the company's statement that passwords and PINs were not leaked holds up.
- Whether the real customer data in the test environment was masked: the company told one outlet it was not, but another reports it is still under investigation.

This is the company's own statement of what it has not found, made while its investigation is continuing, with the words 'at this time'. No outside check exists. ## Related, but separate

| Claim | Label | What we know | Why it supports, and more detail | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whether this breach is linked to Rakuten Group's earlier incidents or to other recent attacks on Japanese securities firms | Not established | The Japan Times notes that Rakuten Travel and Rakuten Drive disclosed separate incidents last month and that other Japanese securities firms reported leaks, but it does not link them to this one. | The Japan Times describes them as separate disclosures and does not connect them. We found no official or independent source tying this breach to any of those incidents. They are listed as context only. | [The Japan Times: Rakuten Securities account information compromised in major data breach](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/11/18/companies/rakuten-securities-unauthorized-access/) |
| A Tokyo law firm is gathering customers for a possible class action against Rakuten Securities | Reported | The Japan Times reports at least 15,000 people had registered interest by Nov 20, according to a lawyer for the claimants. | One Tier 2 outlet, citing the law firm organizing claimants. The firm says it will decide whether to file depending on how many people sign up and what the company does next. No lawsuit had been filed as of that report. The Japan Times also reports the company had not said whether it will compensate customers. | [The Japan Times: Over 15,000 register interest in class action after Rakuten Securities breach](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/11/20/japan/crime-legal/rakuten-securities-lawsuit/) |

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of our latest check on Nov 21.

- A published account of how the attacker got in, or a forensic report. Rakuten Securities says the cause is still under investigation.
- The original Japanese media comments behind the report that the test-environment data was unmasked. Two outlets now report that real data was used (Nov 21), but the company says masking is still under investigation.
- Any named attacker, ransomware or extortion claim, or published data reported by an outlet. We looked only at news coverage and company pages. We did not visit leak sites, dark-web pages or trackers.
- A page of the Financial Services Agency's own about the report order. We found the order through the company's release and Japanese news coverage.
- Any official or independent link to Rakuten Group's other incidents or to other recent attacks on Japanese securities firms.
- Any independent check of the company's statements that passwords and PINs were not leaked and that no related fraudulent trades occurred.
- The company's notices are in Japanese. We translated them ourselves; the Nikkei report is behind a paywall and we did not use it.
